s1.p1: Very often the number of loop iterations is unknown in advance and it depends on the fulfilment of some condition.
s1.p2: As the army saying goes, ‘dig from the fence to lunch’.
s1.p3: That is why we cannot use the iteration counter because we cannot set a limit on its value.
s1.p4: In this case, we use one of the **⟦f0⟧** or **⟦f1⟧** loop operators.
s2.p1: Syntactically, the **⟦f2⟧** operator includes three mandatory parts: the word **⟦f3⟧** itself, followed by parentheses in which the logical expression (the loop condition) will be written, and then the body of the loop enclosed in curly braces:
s2.p2: What will the engine do when faced with such an expression?
s2.p3: 1. First, it will calculate the value of the boolean expression in parentheses and convert it to a boolean type.
s2.p4: 2. If the condition is satisfied (i.e. the calculated value is ⟦f4⟧), the code inside the curly brackets will be executed (the next iteration of the loop).
s2.p5: After that the engine will return to point 1.
